assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hardware correction of spherical aberration made routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy possible, and it underpins atomic-scale structural and chemical analysis across materials physics, interfaces, catalysts and quantum materials. This is a clear invention with a defined original idea, an engineering demonstration and decades of demonstrated consequence. From the perspective of an in situ microscopist, the instrument-enabled discoveries that followed make the impact unusually concrete.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of aberration correctors, Haider led the realisation of the hexapole corrector for the TEM and Urban led the first high-resolution demonstrations and applications at Juelich. This is a coherent three-person configuration. Credit for the STEM corrector (Krivanek and collaborators) is not among the supplied names and is a real allocation question that I cannot resolve from the longlist.
assessment.maturity: The correctors have been in commercial use for roughly two decades, with very strong independent confirmation in thousands of publications. Recognition is not premature; the main timing risk is that the field is aging and some principals are in late career.
uncertainties: Whether the TEM-corrector trio fairly captures the invention given the parallel STEM aberration-correction work that is not in the credited names.
I am relying on memory for dates and for who built which corrector; I have not verified these independently.
The committee may view this as instrumentation whose prize-relevant discovery is spread over many downstream results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the experimental observation of correlated insulator and superconducting states opened the entire field of moire quantum matter. The discovery is original, conceptually clean and has produced a large, fast-growing literature on tunable strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the first experimental demonstration of correlated and superconducting behaviour in magic-angle graphene. The theory-plus-experiment configuration is natural. Cao as lead experimental author and others in the broader moire community are not among the credited names, so allocation of experimental credit within the group is a question.
assessment.maturity: The observations have been reproduced by many groups and extended to other moire systems, so the experimental core is well confirmed. The interpretation of the superconducting mechanism and the full phase diagram remain debated, and recognition could be considered slightly early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of some correlated phases are still unsettled.
Experimental credit is tied to a student-led first demonstration and to other groups' independent work, which may complicate a three-person limit.
Details of the history are recalled from memory and not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength idea, gives fractional uncertainties at the 10^-18 level and opens applications in redefining the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. This is a clear invention with sustained, measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised the strontium lattice clock; Ye brought it to extreme accuracy and stability and developed related spectroscopy. A two-person split is natural, although Hall and Hansen already received credit in 2005 for the frequency comb, and others in ion clocks and in the Boulder community also contributed. Whether a third name from the supplied list is needed is not clear since only two are credited.
assessment.maturity: The performance has been independently confirmed by multiple national laboratories, and the redefinition of the second is under active discussion. The work is mature, with ongoing improvements that do not threaten the central claim.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes (frequency combs, laser cooling) may make some members see this as incremental.
The role of other contributors, such as trapped-ion and Al+ clock groups, is not accounted for in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and was an extraordinary experimental achievement in detectors, data analysis and collaboration. The 2013 prize covered the theory of the mechanism but not the experimental discovery, so a prize for the measurement is scientifically very well justified.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions were made by two collaborations of thousands. The prize statutes allow at most three, and the supplied names include founders and early proponents (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) as well as the spokesperson at discovery (Gianotti). Any choice of three is a judgement about leadership versus decisive technical work and I cannot defend it as uniquely fair.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation by two experiments, measurement of couplings and ongoing LHC data make the discovery fully mature. Timing is not an issue.
uncertainties: The three-laureate limit does not map onto a collective discovery, and the choice of three among four names is contestable.
The committee has traditionally been cautious about prizes that elevate collaboration leaders; I cannot say how this would be weighed.
My selection among the four credited names is a judgement, not verified attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators created a new classification of electronic phases and a large experimental field, with the HgTe quantum well observation giving an early direct demonstration of edge transport. The impact on condensed matter is deep and broad.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant; Molenkamp's group realised and measured it in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and the late Shoucheng Zhang are not among the supplied names, and that gap is an attribution problem. The three-person configuration is plausible but credit for the HgTe prediction is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation in HgTe and in three-dimensional materials is strong, though applications are still developing. The field is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: The omission of the HgTe prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) from the credited names complicates fairness.
The overlap with the separate longlist entry B014, which includes the quantum anomalous Hall effect, means that the configuration of topological insulators could be allocated differently.
Facts are recalled rather than independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO junctions provided the performance needed for hard-disk read heads and magnetic random-access memory. It combines a materials-level insight, coherent spin-dependent tunnelling through epitaxial barriers, with substantial technological use. Interface structure and its control are central, which is a subject close to my own work.
assessment.attribution: Butler and Mathon-Umerski made the theoretical prediction; Yuasa and Parkin independently demonstrated large room-temperature effects in 2004. Mathon and Umerski are not in the supplied names, and Fert and Gruenberg were already recognised for GMR. The three supplied names offer a reasonable split between theory and experiment.
assessment.maturity: The result is very well confirmed and has been in commercial devices for many years. The physics is stable and recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Close temporal priority between Yuasa and Parkin groups needs careful checking.
Theory credit is divided among several authors and only Butler is supplied.
Whether the committee would regard the work as sufficiently distinct from the GMR prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond gave a room-temperature solid-state qubit and a family of nanoscale sensors for magnetic fields, temperature and biology. It is original, widely used and links materials defect physics to quantum technologies.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single-centre detection and coherent control; Lukin contributed a broad programme on NV-based sensing and quantum registers. Other groups (Awschalom, Hanson, Walsworth, Budker) also contributed decisively, and a three-name limit is likely to leave out important people.
assessment.maturity: The methods are reproduced worldwide and are moving into applications, but the field is still growing and sensing applications are not yet fully established, so the timing might be a little early.
uncertainties: Competing contributors outside the supplied names are numerous.
Whether the discovery is the single-defect detection or the broader sensing programme is not clear from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal of photonic band gaps and their experimental realisation changed the design of optical materials and led to photonic-crystal fibres, cavities and nanophotonic devices. The concept is original and has had lasting influence on optics and materials physics.
assessment.attribution: Yablonovitch and John independently proposed the idea in 1987 and Yablonovitch demonstrated the first microwave-scale structure; Russell developed photonic-crystal fibres and Noda realised high-Q nanocavities. A prize for the concept could use the first two names, but this leaves out the fibre and cavity realisation, which is a real allocation tension.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed, with many commercial and research applications, so it is mature. Some experimental promises, such as complete three-dimensional band gaps at optical wavelengths, have been slower to arrive.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the committee would prefer the concept or the applications as the prize-worthy discovery.
Credit is split across several important contributors, and the two-name selection is a judgement.
